widgetData.source_sentence: what is still blocking dead letter replay tooling
sentences:
Dead Letter Queue replay tooling

Operators need a safe way to replay events out of the Dead Letter Queue after a fix ships. Add atlasctl dlq replay backed by api/pipelines.py with filters on pipeline, failure class and time window, a dry-run mode that prints counts only, and a rate limit so replay never starves live traffic. Acceptance criteria: replayed events keep their original event_id so downstream deduplication still holds, every replay writes an audit record, and the runbook contains a worked example from the 2026-08-26 regression. Status history: todo 2026-08-25, in_progress 2026-09-02, in_review 2026-09-09 with two open review comments from Vikram Joshi about rate limiting. Depends on ATLAS-107, ATLAS-108 and ATLAS-116. Reporter Vikram Joshi, assignee Neha Kapoor.

INC-002 Staging Ingestion Outage from SSL Verification Failure

Document kind: incident. Author: Vikram Joshi. Reviewers: Rohan Mehta, Maya Rao, Akshay Sharma. Status: active, written 2026-08-19, reviewed at the postmortem on 2026-08-21. Impact: all staging CDC ingestion down for 4 hours 11 minutes, 2026-08-19T06:12Z to 10:23Z. No customer data was affected; the pilot demo scheduled for that afternoon was postponed. Timeline: 06:12Z connector pods begin crash-looping with certificate verify failed; 06:40Z Vikram Joshi opens ATLAS-110 and states on the bridge that the staging PostgreSQL server certificate has expired; 07:20Z a certificate renewal request is filed with the platform team, which is the wrong remediation; 09:05Z Rohan Mehta checks openssl output and finds the server certificate valid until 2027-01-14; 09:30Z he execs into a pod and finds /etc/ssl/certs/aster-internal-ca.pem absent; 09:40Z ATLAS-111 is opened, tracing the loss to the slim base image adopted on 2026-08-14; 10:23Z a rebuilt image restores ingestion. CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: the expired-server-certificate claim recorded in the first version of ATLAS-110 is incorrect and superseded by ATLAS-111. Corrective actions: CA bundle baked in with a build-time fingerprint assertion and a start-up self-check, per the SSL hardening decision, shipped in PR-004 with commit e42a7f0c3b91; the SSL certificate runbook now mandates checking the client side before the server. 90 minutes of the outage are directly attributable to diagnosing in the wrong order.

ADR-004 Retry Budget and Backoff Policy

Document kind: decision. Author: Vikram Joshi. Approvers: Neha Kapoor, Rohan Mehta, Maya Rao. Status: approved 2026-08-26, implemented 2026-09-01 under ATLAS-108. Context: the first draft of the DLQ replay runbook stated a retry budget of five attempts with a 30 second ceiling. During the retry and DLQ design review Vikram Joshi pointed out that Aster Labs broker maintenance routinely takes eight to twelve minutes, so a 30 second ceiling would exhaust every retry and dump an entire maintenance window into the Dead Letter Queue, turning a self-healing event into a manual replay of tens of thousands of records. Neha Kapoor countered that a long ceiling delays the visibility of genuinely broken pipelines. Decision: eight attempts with exponential backoff and full jitter, base 2 seconds, ceiling 15 minutes, giving roughly 45 minutes of tolerance; and, to answer the visibility concern, a pipeline with any event past attempt four for more than five minutes raises a warning on the Observability Dashboard under ATLAS-119. The earlier five-attempt, 30-second text in the runbook is superseded and the runbook was corrected on 2026-08-27. Implemented in workers/retry_worker.py through PR-005 and commit b8740e2fd1a3, with ceilings configurable in deploy/helm/atlas/values.yaml.

widgetData.source_sentence: what did sprint 1 planning commit to
sentences:
Atlas Sprint 3 planning and release scoping

Agenda: plan the final sprint, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-11, and set a release date for Atlas 1.0. Committed: ATLAS-109 and ATLAS-119 for the Observability Dashboard, ATLAS-123 for the 10k events per second load test, ATLAS-118 for Dead Letter Queue replay tooling, ATLAS-113 once the load test quantifies the checkpoint cost, and ATLAS-124 to run the release gates. Sara Khan proposed 2026-09-04 as the release date so the pilot could be onboarded the following week; Maya Rao and Vikram Joshi both argued that a release date before the load test result is a guess. The date was set to 2026-09-04 anyway and moved to 2026-09-11 four days later once the first load test run failed on latency. Rohan Mehta reported FalkorDB capacity had not materialised, so ATLAS-117 is descoped from 1.0 and continues read-only; Maya Rao accepted this as a documented risk rather than a blocker. Akshay Sharma raised that ATLAS-121, the pilot backfill cutover, depends on a customer maintenance window nobody controls. Decisions: four scope items are the release bar, everything else is optional, and every gate needs a passing test and an owned runbook.

Atlas Sprint 1 planning

Agenda: scope Atlas Sprint 1, confirm the four Project Atlas commitments for the six week run, and name the risks. Maya Rao opened with the shape of the release: PostgreSQL CDC, schema-evolution handling, retry and Dead Letter Queue processing, and an Observability Dashboard. Sara Khan pushed for a pilot customer demo inside three weeks; Maya Rao pushed back because staging still runs PostgreSQL 13 and cannot exercise logical replication at all. That became ATLAS-120, immediately the top risk and, within a day, blocked on a platform maintenance window. Committed to the sprint: ATLAS-101 for the CDC reader, ATLAS-102 for the canonical event envelope, ATLAS-105 for Schema Registry integration, ATLAS-114 for the integration harness and ATLAS-120 for the staging upgrade. Akshay Sharma argued that the envelope has to carry a deterministic event_id from day one, because without it no duplicate or loss claim is measurable; Sara Khan accepted this over a simpler UUID. That argument is written up in the Atlas Event Envelope and Schema Registry Design page and later proved decisive during the duplicate delivery investigation. Neha Kapoor raised that acknowledgement ordering in the reader is unspecified, and it was deferred rather than resolved. Decisions: one replication slot per pipeline, Avro on the wire, and no customer demo until staging runs PostgreSQL 16.

Add PostgreSQL logical replication CDC reader

Repository atlas-connectors, branch feature/ATLAS-101-cdc-reader, author Akshay Sharma, reviewers Maya Rao and Neha Kapoor. Implements ATLAS-101 as agreed in the CDC reader design review on 2026-08-04 and documented in the Atlas PostgreSQL CDC Reader Design page. Adds connectors/postgres/cdc_reader.py with pgoutput decoding, one slot per pipeline named atlas_slot_<pipeline>, bounded reconnect backoff and a slot lag gauge in monitoring/metrics.py. Chart defaults for slot naming and backoff go into deploy/helm/atlas/values.yaml. Review findings: Neha Kapoor flagged that the slot position is acknowledged immediately after the producer call returns; Akshay Sharma noted this as acceptable for the first cut and opened a follow-up, which became the duplicate delivery problem in ATLAS-103. Merged 2026-08-10 after staging soak against the newly upgraded PostgreSQL 16 from ATLAS-120.

Map envelope fields by name across schema generations

Repository atlas-connectors, branch fix/ATLAS-112-name-based-mapping, author Akshay Sharma, reviewers Neha Kapoor, Lina Thomas and Sara Khan. sentences:
FalkorDB lineage graph for Atlas pipeline topology

Persist pipeline topology in FalkorDB so Nilus can answer questions such as which downstream consumers are affected when a source table changes. Nodes are source tables, pipelines, topics and consumers; edges carry schema_version and last_seen_lsn. Acceptance criteria: the graph is rebuilt from the control plane on boot, a table-to-consumer impact query returns in under 200 ms, and the graph is updated on every registration from api/pipelines.py. Status history: todo 2026-08-17, blocked 2026-08-24 waiting on FalkorDB capacity from the platform team, in_progress 2026-09-08 with a reduced scope of read-only lineage. Not in the Atlas 1.0 scope; carried as an accepted risk in the post-release risk register. Depends on ATLAS-116. Reporter Akshay Sharma, assignee Akshay Sharma.

Project Atlas program retrospective and lessons learned

Agenda: close out six weeks of Project Atlas, ATLAS-101 through ATLAS-125, on the day Atlas 1.0 released. Maya Rao facilitated with the whole team and framed it around what generalises beyond this project. Akshay Sharma offered the first lesson: the deterministic event_id decided at Sprint 1 planning under ATLAS-102 is the only reason the duplicate delivery problem was a number rather than a suspicion, so design for observability of correctness, not just health. Neha Kapoor offered the second: both the duplicate events in ATLAS-103 and the latency regression in ATLAS-113 came from where a write sits relative to an acknowledgement rather than from the write itself. Vikram Joshi and Lina Thomas returned to the falsification lesson from the Sprint 2 retrospective, now embedded in the runbooks. Rohan Mehta added that a slim base image is a supply chain change, which is what ATLAS-111 actually was. Sara Khan closed on documentation: the FULL versus BACKWARD dispute in ATLAS-122 and the two competing latency SLOs each cost days purely because two documents disagreed and neither said superseded. Carried forward: the risks in the post-release risk register and the thirty-day monitoring plan in ATLAS-125.

Atlas 1.0 release readiness checklist and go or no-go

Track every gate for the Atlas 1.0 release: CDC reader, schema evolution, retry and Dead Letter Queue processing, and the Observability Dashboard, each with a passing test and an owned runbook. The original target of 2026-09-04 was set at Sprint 3 planning; the date moved to 2026-09-11 after the load test rerun and the DLQ replay tooling in ATLAS-118 stayed in review. Acceptance criteria: all four scope items demonstrated, four runbooks published, SLOs agreed, and remaining risks explicitly accepted by Sara Khan and Maya Rao. Status history: todo 2026-08-31, in_progress 2026-09-04, done 2026-09-11 with a go decision and DLQ replay shipped as a manual procedure. Reporter Sara Khan, assignee Maya Rao.

Runbook: Dead Letter Queue Triage and Replay

That is superseded by the retry policy decision of eight attempts with a 15 minute ceiling under ATLAS-108. Update 2026-09-10: the replay CLI in ATLAS-118 is still in review with open rate-limiting comments, so for Atlas 1.0 replay is performed manually using the worked example from the 2026-08-26 regression, where 312 malformed envelopes were replayed in three batches of 104.

Alert on replication slot growth before disk pressure

A stalled Atlas consumer holds the PostgreSQL replication slot open and retained WAL grows until the primary runs out of disk. Add a slot_retained_bytes gauge to monitoring/metrics.py and page SRE at 20 GB retained or 30 minutes of no slot advance, whichever comes first. Acceptance criteria: the alert fired correctly during the 2026-08-19 SSL outage rehearsal, the on-call runbook documents the drain procedure, and the gauge is visible on the Observability Dashboard. Status history: todo 2026-08-17, in_progress 2026-08-20, done 2026-08-24. Depends on ATLAS-101; feeds ATLAS-109. Reporter Vikram Joshi, assignee Vikram Joshi. Evidence: PR-007 panels and the dashboard on-call runbook.

Add a slot_retained_bytes gauge to monitoring/metrics.py and page SRE at 20 GB retained or 30 minutes of no slot advance, whichever comes first. Acceptance criteria: the alert fired correctly during the 2026-08-19 SSL outage rehearsal, the on-call runbook documents the drain procedure, and the gauge is visible on the Observability Dashboard.
